claim: HeLa cells readjust homeostasis upon proteostatically driven ER stress triggered by inducible bulk expression of secretory immunoglobulin M heavy chain (μs) thanks to the unfolded protein response (UPR; Bakunts et al., 2017).
source: Previously we showed that HeLa cells readjust homeostasis upon proteostatically driven ER stress, triggered by inducible bulk expression of secretory immunoglobulin M heavy chain (μs) thanks to the unfolded protein response (UPR; Bakunts et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Bakunts et al., 2017) that established this finding.

claim: Conditions that prevent restoration of an excess of BiP over µs lead to µs-driven proteotoxicity.
source: Here we show that conditions that prevent that an excess of the ER resident chaperone (and UPR target gene) BiP over µs is restored lead to µs-driven proteotoxicity, i.e. abrogation of HRD1-mediated ER-associated degradation (ERAD), or of the UPR, in particular the ATF6α branch.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing that abrogation of ERAD or UPR (particularly ATF6α) leads to proteotoxicity.

claim: Abrogation of HRD1-mediated ER-associated degradation (ERAD) leads to µs-driven proteotoxicity.
source: Here we show that conditions that prevent that an excess of the ER resident chaperone (and UPR target gene) BiP over µs is restored lead to µs-driven proteotoxicity, i.e. abrogation of HRD1-mediated ER-associated degradation (ERAD), or of the UPR, in particular the ATF6α branch.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing synthetic lethality upon HRD1 ablation in µs-expressing cells.

claim: Abrogation of the UPR, in particular the ATF6α branch, leads to µs-driven proteotoxicity.
source: Here we show that conditions that prevent that an excess of the ER resident chaperone (and UPR target gene) BiP over µs is restored lead to µs-driven proteotoxicity, i.e. abrogation of HRD1-mediated ER-associated degradation (ERAD), or of the UPR, in particular the ATF6α branch.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced viability and growth upon ATF6α silencing in µs-expressing cells.

claim: Conditions that prevent restoration of BiP excess over µs are tolerated upon removal of the BiP-sequestering first constant domain (CH1) from µs.
source: Such conditions are tolerated instead upon removal of the BiP-sequestering first constant domain (CH1) from µs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that µs∆CH1 expression does not cause synthetic lethality upon UPR ablation.

claim: Proteostatic ER stress is a specific consequence of inadequate BiP availability.
source: Thus, our data define proteostatic ER stress to be a specific consequence of inadequate BiP availability, which both the UPR and ERAD redeem.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that ER stress and proteotoxicity correlate with BiP availability relative to µs levels.

claim: Both the UPR and ERAD redeem inadequate BiP availability.

claim: Accumulation of unfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)—a condition referred to as ER stress—activates the unfolded protein response (UPR).
source: It is well-established that accumulation of unfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)—a condition referred to as ER stress—activates the unfolded protein response (UPR), which, in turn, mitigates the stress, most notably through enhancing the ER chaperone content to boost the protein folding capacity (Walter and Ron, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Walter and Ron, 2011).

claim: The two UPR activation models (BiP dissociation and direct binding of unfolded proteins) are not mutually exclusive but complementary and should be unified.
source: Based on insights obtained from µs-driven ER stress, we argue that these two UPR activation models are not mutually exclusive. Rather, the two models are complementary and should be unified, since in a three-way competition between UPR sensors, BiP, and an ER client protein (µs) for binding one another, the ratio of UPR sensors bound to the client versus those bound to BiP most robustly report on the client/BiP ratio, to which indeed the UPR signaling amplitude correlates (Bakunts et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' interpretation of their data and previous findings (Bakunts et al., 2017).

claim: There is no further build-up of µs levels and ER expansion after ~2–3 days once homeostasis is restored.

claim: Co-expression of µs∆CH1 with VL-CH1 restored synthetic lethality upon UPR ablation.
source: Conversely, co-expression of µs∆CH1 with a chimeric protein consisting of the variable domain of λ fused with the CH1 domain of µs (VL-CH1), which teams up with µs∆CH1 through interactions between VL with the variable domain of µs (VH) (Figure 7A), restored UPR activation (Figure 7B) and synthetic lethality upon UPR ablation (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The BiP sequestering CH1 domain of µs causes UPR activation, as well as proteotoxicity when reinforcement of BiP levels through the UPR is inadequate.
source: These findings corroborate that the BiP sequestering CH1 domain of µs causes UPR activation, as well as proteotoxicity when reinforcement of BiP levels through the UPR is inadequate.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that removal of CH1 abolishes UPR activation and synthetic lethality, while adding it back restores both.

claim: The fact that BiP plays a key role in regulating the UPR has been known for almost 20 years.
source: The fact that BiP plays a key role in regulating the UPR has been known for almost 20 years (Bertolotti et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Bertolotti et al., 2000).

claim: Inactivating BiP with the AB5 subtilase cytotoxin acutely causes ER stress and UPR activation.
source: Overexpression of BiP dampens UPR activation (Bertolotti et al., 2000), which we confirm with the data presented here, while inactivating BiP with the AB5 subtilase cytotoxin acutely causes ER stress and UPR activation (Paton et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Paton et al., 2006).

claim: By employment of a proteostatic stimulus with a single well-defined BiP binding module as the source of ER stress, experimental evidence has been provided that defines both proteostatic ER stress, and the resulting activation of the UPR, to be the specific consequence of insufficient BiP availability.
source: Yet, by employment of a proteostatic stimulus with a single well-defined BiP binding module as the source of ER stress, we have provided here experimental evidence that defines both proteostatic ER stress, and the resulting activation of the UPR, to be the specific consequence of insufficient BiP availability.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both the UPR and ERAD redress the relative BiP shortage, and thus counteract that the proteostatic stress becomes proteotoxic.
source: Both the UPR and ERAD redress the relative BiP shortage, and thus counteract that the proteostatic stress becomes proteotoxic.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that both UPR and ERAD are necessary to maintain viability in µs-expressing cells.

claim: BiP has been acclaimed as the master regulator of ER function.
source: BiP indeed has been acclaimed as the master regulator of ER function (Hendershot, 2004), and various cytotoxic consequences may follow from the excessive sequestering of BiP by µs that precludes BiP from attending to its other functions.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Hendershot, 2004).

claim: Various cytotoxic consequences may follow from the excessive sequestering of BiP by µs that precludes BiP from attending to its other functions.
source: BiP indeed has been acclaimed as the master regulator of ER function (Hendershot, 2004), and various cytotoxic consequences may follow from the excessive sequestering of BiP by µs that precludes BiP from attending to its other functions.
evidence: The claim is based on reasoning about the consequences of BiP sequestration.

claim: BiP closes off the translocon, and efflux of Ca2+ from the ER into the cytosol through poorly gated translocons may already be sufficient to cause apoptosis.
source: For instance, BiP closes off the translocon, and efflux of Ca2+ from the ER into the cytosol through poorly gated translocons may already be sufficient to cause apoptosis (Schäuble et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Schäuble et al., 2012).

claim: Proteotoxicity stemming from the accumulation of client proteins in the ER is not the result of UPR signaling.
source: Our data emphasize that proteotoxicity stemming from the accumulation of client proteins in the ER is not the result of UPR signaling, as often is assumed from the notion that the UPR can initiate pro-apoptotic pathways.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that the UPR counteracts rather than causes proteotoxicity.

claim: The UPR foremost counteracts proteotoxicity by inducing the ER resident folding machinery (most in particular BiP).
source: Instead, the UPR foremost counteracts proteotoxicity by inducing the ER resident folding machinery (most in particular BiP).
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that the UPR is necessary to maintain viability in µs-expressing cells by upregulating BiP.

claim: The capacity of the UPR to switch from cytoprotective to pro-apoptotic signaling may well have arisen in metazoans to pre-emptively eliminate cells in which restoration of ER homeostasis is unachievable, and, hence, cell death has become inevitable.
source: In light of our data, the capacity of the UPR to switch from cytoprotective to pro-apoptotic signaling may well have arisen in metazoans to pre-emptively eliminate cells in which restoration of ER homeostasis is unachievable, and, hence, cell death has become inevitable.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the evolutionary origin of UPR pro-apoptotic signaling.

claim: PERK and IRE1α are dispensable for successful ER homeostatic readjustment to the µs stimulus in HeLa cells.
source: Perhaps surprisingly, our results furthermore highlight that PERK and IRE1α are dispensable for successful ER homeostatic readjustment to the µs stimulus in HeLa cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that ablation of PERK and IRE1α does not impair viability or growth in µs-expressing cells.

claim: The PERK-mediated translational block offers negligible advantage when cells face a sudden proteostatic insult that sequesters BiP in a persistent manner.
source: Apparently, the PERK-mediated translational block, which is only transient, offers negligible advantage when cells face a sudden proteostatic insult that sequesters BiP (and/or the ER chaperone machinery at large) in a persistent manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that PERK is dispensable for homeostatic readjustment to µs expression.

claim: PERK-mediated translational attenuation may be required in particular to sustain episodic secretory activity, such as in β-cells of the pancreas.
source: PERK-mediated translational attenuation instead may be required in particular to sustain episodic secretory activity, such as in β-cells of the pancreas.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the role of PERK in different cellular contexts.

claim: PERK KO mice suffer mostly from degeneration of tissues with episodic secretory activity.
source: PERK KO mice indeed suffer mostly from degeneration of tissues with episodic secretory activity (Zhang et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Zhang et al., 2002).

claim: Requirements for the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway seem to be tissue-specific.
source: Similarly, requirements for the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway seem to be tissue-specific.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from literature showing different phenotypes in different tissues.

claim: Both deletion of IRE1α and of XBP1 cause embryonic lethality.
source: Both deletion of IRE1α (Urano et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2005) and of XBP1 (Reimold et al., 2000) cause embryonic lethality, but XBP1 KO mice are rescued with an XBP1 transgene specifically expressed in the liver (Lee et al., 2005), while IRE1α KO mice are rescued when the placenta expresses IRE1α (Iwawaki et al., 2009), and the resulting rescued mice display relatively mild symptoms, that ishyperglycemia, hypoinsulinemia, and decreased antibody titers, despite the lack of IRE1α (Iwawaki et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Urano et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2005; Reimold et al., 2000).

claim: Homeostatic readjustment to ER stress in most mammalian tissues seems to rely mainly on ATF6 proteins (i.e. ATF6α and its related ER stress sensor ATF6β).
source: In line with our findings, homeostatic readjustment to ER stress in most mammalian tissues seems to rely mainly on ATF6 proteins (Wu et al., 2007; Yamamoto et al., 2007), that is ATF6α, and its related ER stress sensor ATF6β.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Wu et al., 2007; Yamamoto et al., 2007).

claim: The ATF6α/β double KO confers embryonic lethality.
source: The ATF6α/β double KO confers embryonic lethality (Yamamoto et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established literature (Yamamoto et al., 2007).

claim: Proteotoxicity due to the accumulation of (mutant) proteins in the ER seems to play a key role in various types of disease.
source: Finally, since proteotoxicity due to the accumulation of (mutant) proteins in the ER seems to play a key role in various types of disease (Anelli and Sitia, 2010; Cao and Kaufman, 2014), our insights may be of relevance for the design of drugs aimed at alleviating ER stress (Hetz and Papa, 2018), and hence proteotoxicity stemming from ER stress.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Anelli and Sitia, 2010; Cao and Kaufman, 2014).

claim: Pharmacological intervention against pathogenic ER stress foremost should promote a favorable ratio of BiP levels over those of its disease-causing client protein.
source: We argue that pharmacological intervention against pathogenic ER stress foremost should promote a favorable ratio of BiP levels over those of its disease-causing client protein.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' interpretation of their findings and represents a recommendation for therapeutic approaches.
